title: Nut-Free Chocolate Chip Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes studded with mini chocolate chips, ready in about 43 minutes from prep to cooling.
description: These cupcakes are soft, tender, and safe for nut-free kitchens or classrooms. Mini chocolate chips stay evenly spread through the batter instead of sinking to the bottom.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add flour mix in three parts, alternating with milk and sour cream. Mix just until smooth.
Toss mini chocolate chips with 1 tablespoon flour. Fold into batter by hand so they spread evenly.
Divide batter into liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, beat butter on its own for 2 minutes until pale and smooth.
Add powdered sugar one cup at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt. Beat 2 more minutes until fluffy.
Pipe or spread frosting on fully cooled cupcakes. Top with a few extra mini chips if you like.
tips: Toss the chips in flour before folding them in. This keeps them from sinking to the bottom of the pan.
Use room temperature eggs and milk so the batter mixes evenly and stays smooth.
Do not overmix once the flour goes in. Overmixing makes the crumb tough instead of soft.
Always double check that your chocolate chip brand is processed in a nut-free facility if allergies are a concern.

faq.question: Why do my chocolate chips sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: Chips sink when the batter is too thin or the chips are too heavy for the mix. Tossing mini chips in a little flour before folding them in helps them stay suspended through baking.

faq.question: Are mini chocolate chips actually nut-free?
faq.answer: Not always, so check the label. Many mainstream brands are made nut-free, but some are processed on shared lines with tree nuts.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the day you plan to serve them for the best texture.

faq.question: Why is my cupcake texture dense instead of soft?
faq.answer: Dense cupcakes usually come from overmixing the batter or measuring too much flour. Spoon flour into the cup and level it off instead of scooping straight from the bag.

conclusion: These cupcakes work for birthdays, bake sales, or any nut-free classroom. Soft crumb, even chips, and a simple buttercream make them easy to repeat.
